responsibility: This tutorial example is the minimal C-language demonstration of libgccjit’s in-memory compilation flow. It builds a context, declares an imported printf and an exported greet function, emits a single basic block calling printf with a string literal and parameter, compiles the context to machine code, retrieves the generated symbol with gcc_jit_result_get_code, and executes it. Its purpose is to show the smallest end-to-end use of the C API.
same_name_distinction: Unlike gcc/jit/docs/examples/tut01-hello-world.cc, this same-stem tutorial uses the plain C libgccjit API from libgccjit.h, with explicit gcc_jit_* handles and calls rather than the C++ wrapper classes from libgccjit++.h.
